figures.caption: DC drive compliance of the control amplifier at the typical corner, as a map of the unity-gain tracking error over commanded output voltage and load current. Positive $I_{\mathrm{LOAD}}$ draws current out of the output, so the amplifier \emph{sources}; negative $I_{\mathrm{LOAD}}$ injects, so it \emph{sinks}. The colour scale is clipped at \(\pm\SI{50}{\milli\volt}\), the compliance criterion: inside the envelope the error is the smooth $I_{\mathrm{LOAD}}R_{\mathrm{O}}$ gradient, and outside it the output has hit a rail, so everything beyond the envelope saturates to solid colour. The two black curves are the \(|V_{\mathrm{OUT}}-V_{\mathrm{MAP}}|=\SI{50}{\milli\volt}\) edges, interpolated on the \SI{50}{\nano\ampere} sweep at each of the 26 commanded voltages. The vertical axis is cropped to \(\pm\SI{8}{\micro\ampere}\). Numerical values are in Table~\ref{tab:ctrlamp-drivemap}.

Width of the \(\pm\SI{50}{\milli\volt}\) compliance envelope against commanded output voltage, over all five process corners. The shape is the same in every corner: pinched at both ends of the output range and widest around \SI{1.8}{\volt}. The vertical scale is clipped at \SI{16}{\micro\ampere}; outside roughly \SIrange{0.3}{1.9}{\volt} the buffer no longer tracks its input at zero load, and the span plotted there is the current that forces the output onto the commanded value.

tables.caption: Drive compliance against commanded output voltage at the typical corner, \SI{27}{\celsius}, \SI{2.5}{\volt}, \texttt{BiasAdj}~=~37. Columns: $V_{\mathrm{MAP}}$ commanded output voltage; $I_{\mathrm{SNK}}$ and $I_{\mathrm{SRC}}$ the load currents at which the tracking error reaches \(\mp\SI{50}{\milli\volt}\), positive current being sourced by the amplifier; $\Delta I$ the span between them; $V_{\mathrm{E0}}$ the tracking error at zero load; $R_{\mathrm{O}}$ the closed-loop output resistance, taken as the central difference over \(\pm\SI{0.5}{\micro\ampere}\) about zero load; $I_{\mathrm{DD}}$ the bench supply current. Where $|V_{\mathrm{E0}}|$ exceeds \SI{50}{\milli\volt} the buffer does not track its input at any load, and $I_{\mathrm{SNK}}$/$I_{\mathrm{SRC}}$ are then the external current that forces the output onto the commanded value.
